arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Schnapper argued Shaw jurisprudence guides the current debate. He identified two constitutional claims regarding race in districting.
General Verrilli stated Shaw claims require district-specific analysis. He argued the district court departed from this principle.
Mr. Pildes claimed Alabama used rigid racial quotas. He stated the state used only racial data to meet targets with precision.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Alabama redrew its legislative districts using rigid racial quotas. The state claims this prevented the dilution of minority voting power. Plaintiffs argue the state used race as the primary factor in districting. This practice may violate the Equal Protection Clause.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Plaintiffs argue Alabama used rigid racial quotas to design districts. They claim the state relied solely on racial demographic data to meet targets.
The state argues it moved people to avoid retrogression. It claims it maintained specific black population percentages to protect minority voting effectiveness.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Scalia asked if the state merely moved people to maintain population percentages. He questioned if this avoided retrogression.
Justice Kennedy asked if a party changing districts to undo prior actions creates a violation. He questioned the motive behind partisan balance changes.
